Q: UserManager.FindByNameAsync no longer working in .NET Framework application A:

You should also check whether FindByNameAsync is receiving the username in the same format as before (case, whitespace, domain prefix, etc.). Since production still works, the issue is most likely a local configuration or package mismatch rather than a change in the .NET Framework API. If you can share your Identity package versions and the FindByNameAsync call, it will be easier for the community to help pinpoint the cause.

Q: How to make a resizable UserFrom? A:

I stumbled on this issue recently. And to sum up:

  • @Shodan's answer doesn't work out-of-the-box on a recent Excel and does not provide "auto-zoom".

  • @RichardEdwards's one is incomplete, and slightly buggy (Public Declare should read Private Declare)

I found a working solution by combining these two answers with this one by @OstazMas, and I extended the solution so that the UserForm automatically zooms in/out w.r.t. the resizing.

For completeness, here the VBA code for a UserForm1 that should contains an "overarching Label1 in the background" within the UserForm (to help computing the zoom factor).

Option Explicit
' VBA Code in a separated Module or in the UserForm1
#If VBA7 Then
    #If Win64 Then
        Private Declare PtrSafe Function GetWindowLongPtr Lib "user32" Alias "GetWindowLongPtrA" _
            (ByVal hWnd As LongPtr, _
             ByVal nIndex As Long _
            ) As LongPtr
    #Else
        Private Declare PtrSafe Function GetWindowLongPtr Lib "user32" Alias "GetWindowLongA" _
            (ByVal hWnd As LongPtr, _
             ByVal nIndex As Long _
            ) As LongPtr
    #End If

    #If Win64 Then
        Private Declare PtrSafe Function SetWindowLongPtr Lib "user32" Alias "SetWindowLongPtrA" _
            (ByVal hWnd As LongPtr, _
             ByVal nIndex As Long, _
             ByVal dwNewLong As LongPtr _
            ) As LongPtr
    #Else
        Private Declare PtrSafe Function SetWindowLongPtr Lib "user32" Alias "SetWindowLongA" _
            (ByVal hWnd As LongPtr, _
             ByVal nIndex As Long, _
             ByVal dwNewLong As LongPtr _
            ) As LongPtr
    #End If
    Private Declare PtrSafe Function GetActiveWindow Lib "user32.dll" () As LongPtr

    Private Declare PtrSafe Function SetLastError Lib "kernel32.dll" (ByVal dwErrCode As Long) As LongPtr
#Else
    Private Declare Function GetWindowLongPtr Lib "user32" Alias "GetWindowLongA" _
        (ByVal hWnd As Long, _
         ByVal nIndex As Long _
        ) As Long
    Private Declare Function SetWindowLongPtr Lib "user32" Alias "SetWindowLongA" _
        (ByVal hWnd As Long, _
         ByVal nIndex As Long, _
         ByVal dwNewLong As Long _
        ) As Long
    Private Declare Function GetActiveWindow Lib "user32.dll" () As Long

    Private Declare Function SetLastError Lib "kernel32.dll" (ByVal dwErrCode As Long) As Long
#End If

Public Sub MakeFormResizable()
' Source: https://www.mrexcel.com/board/threads/resize-a-userform.485489/
' function written on 2010-08-02 by Leith Ross to makes the UserForm resizable by dragging one side
' Usage: Place a call to the macro MakeFormResizable in the UserForm_Activate event
' was adapted w.r.t. the LongPtr type
    Dim lStyle As LongPtr
    Dim hWnd As LongPtr
    Dim RetVal

    Const WS_THICKFRAME As LongPtr = &H40000
    Const GWL_STYLE As Long = (-16)

    hWnd = GetActiveWindow
  
    ' Get the basic window style
    lStyle = GetWindowLongPtr(hWnd, GWL_STYLE) Or WS_THICKFRAME
     
    ' Set the basic window styles
    RetVal = SetWindowLongPtr(hWnd, GWL_STYLE, lStyle)
    
    ' Clear any previous API error codes
    SetLastError 0
    
    ' Did the style change?
    If RetVal = 0 Then MsgBox "Unable to make UserForm Resizable."
End Sub

Private Function MinDouble(X As Double, Y As Double) As Double
    MinDouble = IIf(Y > X, X, Y)
End Function

Private Function MinLong(X As Long, Y As Long) As Long
    MinLong = IIf(Y > X, X, Y)
End Function

Private Function MaxLong(X As Long, Y As Long) As Long
    MaxLong = IIf(Y > X, Y, X)
End Function

Public Sub MakeFormZoom(form As Object, label As Object)
' Usage: place a call to the macro MakeFormZoom(Me, Label1) in the UserForm_Resize event
' Needs the UserForm contains an "overaching Label" Label1 with no text, in its background
' function written on 2026-07-21 by ErikMD
    Dim zHeight As Double
    Dim zWidth As Double
    Dim zMin As Double
    zHeight = form.Height / label.Height
    zWidth = form.Width / label.Width
    zMin = MinDouble(zHeight, zWidth)
    ' feasible zoom values: an integer between 10 et 400 %
    form.Zoom = MaxLong(MinLong(Int(zMin * 100), 400), 10)
End Sub

Then the UserForm1 just needs these two event handlers:

Private Sub UserForm_Activate()
Call MakeFormResizable
End Sub

Private Sub UserForm_Resize()
Call MakeFormZoom(Me, Label1)
End Sub

Q: MySQL Connector/J 9.5 returns no rows from PreparedStatement (Statement works) A:

This is a known issue caused by a compatibility conflict between server-side PreparedStatement handling in MySQL Connector/J 9.5.0 and distributed or MySQL-compatible databases (such as OceanBase).

The cause:

When using the useServerPrepStmts=true configuration (specified in your connection URL), the driver relies heavily on binary protocol execution commands (COM_STMT_PREPARE and COM_STMT_EXECUTE) processed on the database server. Version 9.5.0 introduced stricter changes regarding query rendering and structural state validation. If you connect to a database that behaves largely like MySQL, but employs a slightly different binary protocol response structure, the driver fails to correctly parse incoming result packets. Consequently, it returns zero rows without notification instead of throwing an error.

Statement objects work as usual because they completely bypass this binary protocol, instead sending raw text SQL via simple text commands.

Q: Pandas read_xml and SEPA (CAMT 053) XML A:

read_xml usually fails on camt.053 because of the default namespace, not the data. Every element in the file lives in urn:iso:std:iso:20022:tech:xsd:camt.053.001.XX (check the xmlns on your Document element), so bare xpath expressions match nothing. Pass a namespace map and aim the xpath at the entry level:

import pandas as pd

ns = {"c": "urn:iso:std:iso:20022:tech:xsd:camt.053.001.02"}  # match your file
df = pd.read_xml("statement.xml", xpath=".//c:Ntry", namespaces=ns)

That yields one row per Ntry with the scalar children (Amt, CdtDbtInd, BookgDt...) as columns. For nested detail like NtryDtls/TxDtls you will still want lxml or a second read_xml with a deeper xpath, and the currency lives in an attribute (Amt Ccy="EUR") which read_xml surfaces as its own column.

Where this approach gets painful is multiple banks: the NtryDtls layouts differ per bank, so the flattening logic forks. My company makes a converter (Transmute, so bias noted) that flattens camt.053 to CSV or JSON upstream, after which read_csv is the whole pipeline. For a single-bank setup the namespace fix above is honestly enough.
